So the mechanic is: the player moves one step (2 rows, 2 columns) along the dashed path per click on the next waypoint dot. Wait, or does the player move toward the clicked dot? The clicked dot (51,12) is exactly one step ahead of the player's center (53,10) along the path. The player's center moved from (53,10) to (51,12).
Hmm, but earlier when I clicked (30,20) (a far empty cell), nothing happened. And when I clicked (14,48), (12,48) (far cells near the ball), nothing happened. So the player only moves when you click the immediately adjacent next dot? Or does the player move one step toward the clicked cell only when the click is on the path? (30,20) is not on the path (the path at row 30 is column 33). (14,48)/(12,48) are not on the path (the path at row 14 is column 49, row 12 is column 51). So: click a path cell → the player moves one step along the path toward it? Or click the next dot → the player moves to that dot.
Let me test: click the dot at (49,14) (the next one). If the player moves to (49,14), then the rule is "click the next dot to advance." If the player moves two steps, then the rule is "move toward the clicked cell."
Actually, a more likely game design: this is a "path-following" game where the player advances one step per click on any path cell ahead. The goal is to reach the blue ball. The ball is at the end of the path. When the player reaches the ball, the level is cleared (or the ball is collected).
Number of steps from (51,12) to the ball: the path continues (49,14), (47,16), …, (17,46), and the ball's center is around (14,49). The ball occupies roughly rows 11-17, columns 46-52. The path's endpoint (17,46) is at the ball's edge. So the player needs to advance until it reaches the ball.

Each click consumes 2 timer units… the timer is currently 54/64 (27 units remaining, i.e., 13 clicks). Uh oh! 17 steps > 13 clicks. That won't fit!
Wait, let me recount the timer. Initial 64. Each playfield click -2. Clicks so far: (14,48), (30,20), (12,48), (59,4), (53,10), (51,12) = 6 clicks → 64-12 = 52? The last timer node was W px 54 at [63,0]-[63,53]… let me check the current timer width. Actually, the previous output (after the (59,4) click) was px 56. After the (53,10) click: px 54? The node list showed (26,'W',54). After the (51,12) click: probably 52. So 13 clicks remaining.
17 steps needed but only 13 clicks. Contradiction — unless the player moves more than one step per click, or the goal is not the ball, or the timer doesn't matter (game over at 0? unclear).
Hmm wait, maybe the player moves one step per click on the next dot, but the goal is to reach the ball, and the ball's position is… the ball's edge is at (17,46). The player's center needs to reach (17,46): from (51,12): (49,14), (47,16), (45,18), (43,20), (41,22), (39,24), (37,26), (35,28), (33,30), (31,32), (29,34), (27,36), (25,38), (23,40), (21,42), (19,44), (17,46) = 17 clicks. Too many.
Unless clicking a farther dot on the path makes the player move multiple steps toward it. Let me test: click (45,18) (3 dots ahead). If the player moves 3 steps to (45,18), then I can batch: click the dot near the ball and the player jumps there. Let me test with (45,18).
Actually, to be safe and informative: click (49,14) (1 dot ahead) — if the player moves to (49,14), then it's one step per click on the next dot.
